 * names and what they reach, a set of values and the laws they satisfy. It answers what is determined by what: the
 * closure of a body of claims, and the extension of a form.
 *
 * Which operation answers this view is read off the laws its vectors fix: the view an operation has is the view of
 * the laws that name the vectors it ran on, or of the definition it implements. An operation no law reaches keeps the
 * view it was given by hand, as drift. Nothing here is new algebra: every name is re-exported once.

 * view it was given by hand, as drift. Nothing here is new algebra: every name is re-exported once.

 * Who stands beside whom: two cells are one step apart when an origin looked at both, so a world is a graph of the
 * lookings that cross it. A bound is not a looking: cells rest on it without anyone having been to both, so it is
 * named apart and carries no step. What no looking crosses to is past the horizon, and no number reaches it, which
 * is what a horizon returns. A distance is a value of the form the world gives it: no walk in a field of n cells is
 * longer than n steps, so n is that form's top and it is what unreachable reads as, never an absence.
 "

bound-lock/1 at=place:vectors/measure.json by=reader form=alphabet measure=text role=reads scope=said/about value="What conserves, and where.

`complexity` counts how much a statement says, and that count is preserved
when two statements are put together: what BOTH require plus what EITHER
accepts equals the sum of the parts. It is inclusion-exclusion, and it is
what makes the count a measure rather than an index.

On ideals the count conserves on every finite poset: the up-sets of any
poset form a distributive lattice. `isDistributive` still reports whether

ON A LADDER THIS LAW IS TRIVIAL. For a total order the highest and lowest
of two levels are just those two levels again, so ANY weighting satisfies

ones off a ladder. M3 now conserves because the valuation counts excluded
levels of a declared Ω, not irreducibles."

bound-lock/1 at=place:samples/yes/obligatory.json by=reader form=alphabet measure=text role=reads scope=said/about value="The object, with the cases it has to pass before any code is written for it.
A cell is two poles on a lattice it is given, never a lattice it assumes: the same cell folds over an interval, an alphabet and a ladder, and the state it is in is the one that lattice names.
A signature narrows a bound and every cell resting on that bound reads the narrower one; no origin's claim is edited by it, and the order signatures arrive in never shows.
A withdrawal names the claim it takes back, not a value that looks like it, and fold by phase adds claims at one turn of the period as the square of their number.
All four corners are reached: one origin that pins a level is REQUIRED, two that leave the scale open are FREE, two that touch under a ceiling below the top are FORBIDDEN, and two that cannot both hold are CONFLICT.
The object, written down once: two poles read at a resolution, origins that carry the epoch they spoke at and a sign, and an order of rest against other cells.
Five operations answer for it and there are no others. Meet is what the origins hold together, encounter is how many met and what that makes, observe is one more origin at a cost, sign is a bound narrowed wherever it is rested on, refine is the same cell read at another resolution.
A withdrawal takes back its own write and nothing else, so a cell that was written and withdrawn at one epoch is a cell nobody claimed.
Eight acts in four pairs answer for it under seven names, each an offer with a descriptor, and what a descriptor forces is derived from it and refused: a widening that travels, a floor required past a signed ceiling, a withdrawal that leaves its pole where the claim put it, and an order of rest that returns to itself."

bound-lock/1 at=place:vectors/blocks.json by=reader form=alphabet measure=text role=reads scope=said/about value="meetBlocks groups the join-irreducibles of [u ^ w, u v w] by COMPARABILITY,
and priceByBlocks prices each group. This is the localisation pair.

On a chain every irreducible is comparable to every other, so there is always
exactly ONE block: a case built only on a chain cannot tell a correct
partition from any other.

And every obvious valuation — index, index squared — is SUPERMODULAR, and
monotone with supermodular gives g = 0. A file built from those alone reports
zero premiums everywhere while looking thorough. `pricesAnything` exists to
say so: the runner calls it, and a case claiming a premium on a valuation
that prices nothing is refused.

Which lattices have anything to localise:

  A BLOCK CONTRIBUTES A NON-ZERO PREMIUM ONLY IF THE SUBLATTICE IT GENERATES
  CONTAINS AN INCOMPARABLE PAIR — for a MONOTONE INCREASING valuation, which
  is the shape a design scale has, since worth rises with level. There
  `priceByBlocks` returns 0 on all 81 pairs of a 9-rung chain, and the
  spectrum collapses to {0}.

The condition is monotone, not every. A DECREASING valuation gives a non-zero
premium in 79 of those 81 pairs and a sawtooth one in 62. And `premium` and
`gap` are two quantities rather than one: on the same chain `gap` is 0 in
81/81 for an increasing valuation and non-zero in 64/81 for a decreasing one.

RI <= 0 does not license `g == 0` on its own. Monotone AND supermodular gives
zero counterexamples while either half alone leaves many, and among MONOTONE
valuations `g != 0` iff not supermodular, exactly. `pricesAnything` carries
both halves; `!isSupermodular` is IDENTICALLY FALSE on a chain, so a runner
that checks only that half passes vacuously.

B2 and M3 fall there for the plainest reason available: all their
join-irreducibles are atoms, so every pair meets at bottom, so every block is
a singleton, so every block generates the 2-chain {bottom, x}. Add a STEM —
one level between bottom and the atoms — and the atoms meet above bottom, the
block has something to price, and the localised total reconciles exactly.
That pair of cases is below, and it is what makes this a theorem rather than
a shrug.

A board that is a PRODUCT OF SCALES has its irreducibles only on the axes, so
two from different axes meet at bottom, so the blocks ARE the axes and each
axis is a chain. `priceByBlocks` is therefore identically zero on a product
of chains. B2 and M3 are not pathological corners; they are the smallest
members of that family."

bound-lock/1 at=place:samples/yes/T45-cells-that-rest-on-one-bound-are-entangled.json by=reader form=alphabet measure=text role=reads scope=said/about value="Cells that rest on one bound move together when it moves: narrowing a ceiling from a hundred to sixty turned cells red with nobody looking at them, some of them past the horizon of whoever signed it.

bound-lock/1 at=place:samples/yes/T46-a-bound-moves-cells-no-walk-reaches.json by=reader form=alphabet measure=text role=reads scope=said/about value="A world has two physics at once. Looking travels: it reaches what a walk of shared lookings reaches and stops at the horizon.
A bound does not travel: it carries no step and no distance, and moving it changes cells past that horizon in one act.
Counting the bound as if it were a looking would make the whole world one neighbourhood, which is how the two are told apart.
The two physics side by side, in one world of a hundred cells. Looking is local: it reaches seventy-three cells, one step at a time, stops at the horizon, and moves a floor.
Signing is not: it reaches the sixty-six cells that rest on the bound, at no distance, past any horizon, and moves a ceiling. Seven of the cells it turned are cells no looking from the observer could have reached."

bound-lock/1 at=place:vectors/field-uses.json by=reader form=alphabet measure=text role=reads scope=said/about value="The field is the lattice and the debit in motion. Each origin at a point holds a band on a scale — the floor it demands, the ceiling it allows — and the point's declaration is their fold: the demand is the join of the floors, the limit the meet of the ceilings.
A point's state is one of the debit's four, and green, grey, red and fork are its renders (FREE, REQUIRED, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT). The register read at the point gives every debit's state; a declaration is in conflict exactly when some debit is (the debit).
The premium of the point's declaration is the gap; under a supermodular valuation it vanishes on every declaration. A region withdraws exactly when its scale is distributive. What moved between two readings is counted debit by debit.
Nothing here is new algebra: every reading is an operation of lattice/ or debit/ applied to a point of field/."

bound-lock/1 at=place:vectors/encounter.json by=reader form=alphabet measure=text role=reads scope=said/about value="A point is a place where origins can coincide: its state is the set of origins that touched it, with the span each

It got its own file because reconciliation is an industry: with relations stored and coincidence searched afterwards,
asking whether two origins saw one thing costs a pass over everything; here it costs reading one set."

bound-lock/1 at=place:samples/yes/T49-amplitude-has-sign-and-phase.json by=reader form=alphabet measure=text role=reads scope=said/about value="A claim carries a size and a direction: how much it narrows, and the turn of the period it landed on. A withdrawal is the same size pointing the other way.
Two hundred claims in phase make ten thousand — the square of their number — and the same two hundred strewn across the period make sixty-four, of the order of their number.
A write and its withdrawal at one epoch leave nothing; at different epochs they do not cancel.
Thirty-two claims of no width, so each carries an amplitude of one: in phase they make a thousand and twenty-four, which is their number squared, and strewn across the period they make fifty, of the order of their number.
The fringe of four claims half a period apart runs from nothing at no delay to four at half the period and back."

bound-lock/1 at=place:vectors/closure.json by=reader form=alphabet measure=text role=reads scope=said/about value="Combining must accept its own output.

`compose` rejects a statement that was already impossible on its own — a
floor above its own ceiling is a typo, and calling it a collision hides
it. That check is right at the front door and wrong everywhere else: it
made `compose` REFUSE ITS OWN RESULT the moment two statements collided.

An operation that cannot take its own output back is not closed, and
without closure there is exactly one legal way to evaluate: a single pass
over the original statements. No folding in a tree, no combining partial
results from shards, no merging replicas that were partitioned. The whole
reason this arithmetic is worth having is that order does not matter, and
an operation you can only apply left to right does not deliver that.

So `fuse` carries the law and `compose` is `fuse` plus an entry check.
The five properties below are the merge law of a conflict-free replicated
type, which is why a crossed result must survive rather than be resolved
away: both sides were load-bearing, and a winner is not an answer."

bound-lock/1 at=place:vectors/shuffle.json by=reader form=alphabet measure=text role=reads scope=said/about value="A deterministic shuffle, and the two ways one stops being a control.

THE FIRST is the closed form that cancels the salt:
  j = (salt + i*17 + salt*i) % (i + 1)
looks salted, but salt + salt*i is salt*(i+1), which is zero modulo i+1.
The salt cancels identically, so sixty-four draws are ONE permutation drawn
sixty-four times. `varies` is the case that catches it.

THE SECOND is the position-only rule, live until this vector existed:
  j = (salt + i*17) % (i + 1)
does not cancel, but j depends only on the position and the salt — never on
the data, never on a stream. Both call sites passed salt = 3, so there was
exactly one null corpus, ever. And j collapses to 0 whenever i+1 divides 14.
`degenerate` is that case, stated as the thing a shuffle must not be.

AND THE LIMIT, which is not a bug in the shuffle but in what it is asked to
falsify: a permutation preserves the multiset exactly, so it cannot falsify
any claim that is a function of the multiset alone — a floor, a ceiling, a
congruence, a concentration. Finding the law again on shuffled values is
evidence the null was wrong, not that the law is false. `blind` pins the
three quantities that survive, so a miner can refuse to build a control that
would fire on the truth."

bound-lock/1 at=place:vectors/hypothesis.json by=reader form=alphabet measure=text role=reads scope=said/about value="isSupermodular is half of the hypothesis that makes g vanish, and the

The comment read: "RI <= 0 on every pair: then g == 0." On a total order
{x OR y, x AND y} is {x, y}, so RI is identically zero for every valuation.
The predicate cannot say no where it is used.

A vacuous predicate has no symptom. The only way to find one is to ask
whether it CAN disagree - which is what `vacuity.ts` does.

Neither half suffices alone. Among monotone valuations the converse holds:
